summary: Most of the video logic is the shared Capcom (GnG-family) object and tile pipeline, and it is board-shaped. An OKOUT-strobed DMA copies object RAM under 68000 bus arbitration, each line runs a Y-match search into a double line buffer, and tile/char fetches are timed from H counter phases. None of it looks like MAME's frame-batch draw_sprites/screen_update. The SF-specific glue is thin and mostly memory-map work. A few pieces repeat MAME semantics directly: the sprite-code invert() XOR, the MCU address remap and the input port layout. Some pieces depart from MAME: the MCU takes the bus by bus request, the main CPU interrupt comes from the raster counter, and the ADPCM IRQ comes from the MSM5205.

findings.signal: OKOUT-triggered sprite DMA with bus request/ack
findings.note: A write to the c0001a register raises OKOUT. That starts a BR/BGACK bus-grab state machine on the 68000 (jtframe_68kdma), and a counter then copies object RAM into a private buffer during vblank. MAME just reads m_objectram directly at draw time.

findings.signal: Per-line object search + double line buffer
findings.note: Each scanline scans the DMA buffer with an adder-based Y compare (~VF + const + Y, MATCH on the top bits) and copies up to 32 matching objects into a line table. Pixels go into ping-pong line buffers that are cleared on readout. MAME instead loops back-to-front over all 128 sprites per frame.

findings.signal: Large sprites via repeated line-table entry and adders, not MAME's c/c+1/c+16/c+17 quad
findings.note: A 32x32 sprite is a second line-table entry with X+16 and an MSB marker. The tile code is id + 16*(vflip^Vsum[4]) + hflip-dependent 1, computed per line. MAME draws four gfx elements with pointer-swaps for flips. The structure is different even though the arithmetic agrees.

findings.signal: Sprite code XOR identical to MAME invert()
findings.note: The code does 'if(idalt[4]!=idalt[3]) idalt[4:3]=~idalt[4:3]'. That is exactly MAME's nb ^ delta[(nb>>3)&3] with delta {0,0x18,0x18,0}. It is a software ROM-order fixup carried over rather than board wiring.

findings.signal: Tile fetch pipeline from H-counter phases
findings.note: The scroll layer adds hpos to hscan to get {PIC,SH}. The map ROM address is latched at SH[2:0]==6, gfx ROM addresses are issued on HS[2:0] phases, and pixels come out of 4-bit plane shift registers. That is a scan-time pipeline with board-style signal names (SH, SV, PIC, HS), not MAME's tilemap callbacks.

findings.signal: Map ROM addressing matches tilemap scan order
findings.note: The map address {PIC,SH[8:4],SV[7:4]} is column-major like TILEMAP_SCAN_COLS, with attr/code split across ROM halves. Any correct core has to follow this ROM layout.

findings.signal: Fixed layer priority mux equals MAME draw order
findings.note: Priority is fixed as char > obj > scr1 > scr2, with transparency at pen 3 / pen 15, and it feeds a palette RAM. The priority-PROM ports are commented out. This is the same order as MAME's screen_update. It is simple, and either source could produce it.

findings.signal: MCU address remap and strobe bits mirror MAME prot_ram/prot_p3_w
findings.note: Aeff={2'b11,{6{a15}},a} reproduces MAME's '0xff8000|off' vs '0xc00000|off' choice. P3.4 is the byte select (m_prot_t0) and P3.1 clears INT0, matching prot_p3_w. A correct core needs these semantics, but here they are written in MAME's form.

findings.signal: MCU takes the bus via 68000 BR/BGACK arbitration
findings.note: Writing c0001e pulses DMAONn. The MCU INT0 line also serves as a bus request into the same arbiter as the object DMA, and the MCU then drives the shared address/data bus. MAME simply HALTs the main CPU and pokes its address space.

findings.signal: Raster-derived main interrupt and MSM-derived ADPCM IRQ
findings.note: The 68000 interrupt request comes from V counter values (0x70/0xF0) and is acknowledged on FC=111 with VPA. The ADPCM Z80 IRQ is the jt5205 sample-strobe edge. MAME uses an abstract vblank callback and a fixed 8 kHz timer.

findings.signal: Memory map and input ports laid out as MAME ports
findings.note: The address decode is a case on A[23:20] and A[3:1] that matches MAME's map. The inputs are packed IN0/IN1/IN2/SYS like the MAME ports, with a cabcfg switch for the SFJ layout. A correct core has to share this map.
